comparator.name: Pharmaceutical Sciences (Farmaceutische Wetenschappen)
comparator.sourceNotes: The 2026–2027 regulations list 60 EC in each of years one and two, then 12 EC of taught requirements, an 18 EC project and 30 EC of electives. The current regulations govern exact course names and year allocations. The laboratory safety module, Dutch diagnostic or remedial language work and mentoring add no credits. The binding first-year recommendation normally requires 42 EC. The basic pharmacochemistry lab must be passed before the bioanalytical chemistry, molecular pharmacology, synthesis, molecular toxicology and molecular modelling practicals. The usual periods 5–6 project requires all first-year courses, all specified practicals including molecular modelling, and 120 EC including electives. The exceptional periods 2–3 project requires all other courses passed by 31 August of the preceding academic year. The project normally includes experimental research, a lab journal, a thesis, a talk and a poster. Four assessment categories count equally and each requires at least 5.5. The elective period normally needs approval, except for listed minors or other specified exemptions. It permits up to 6 EC at level 100 and requires at least 12 EC at level 300. Chemistry- and biology-focused minors are elective directions.

exception.reason: UCR offers pharmacology, biochemistry and laboratory work on cells and proteins. Students can study drug targets, drug action and how the body processes medicines. VU builds on these topics with a sequence in organic synthesis, compound identification, bioanalysis, toxicology and molecular modelling for drug discovery. UCR’s available courses do not offer that sequence or a comparably sustained focus on discovering and testing new compounds.

exception.ucrCourseEvidence: The active workbook supports one direct Pharmacology course, alongside molecular cell biology, biochemistry and molecular laboratory work. The strengthened 24-course challenge adds chemical testing, materials analysis, metal separation and geochemical speciation. Those are relevant scientific methods with different study objects. The later courses remain centred on biomedical mechanisms, environmental chemistry and general methods. They do not sustain experimental drug discovery.

candidateAssessment.label: Molecular disease, pharmacology and biomedical research
candidateAssessment.reason: Pharmacology directly covers drug targets, pharmacodynamics, pharmacokinetics, metabolism, toxicity and therapeutic applications. Biochemistry, cell biology and laboratory work support molecular mechanisms and experiments. The sustained study centres on how disease and existing therapies work. It does not build towards design, synthesis and evaluation of new compounds.

candidateAssessment.label: Drug discovery through chemistry and analysis
candidateAssessment.reason: The strongest feasible chemistry-augmented 180 EC attempt includes spectroscopy and chemical testing, metal recovery and separation, and speciation and geochemical modelling. Alongside drug targets and biomolecular lab work these give genuine methodological overlap. The practical sequence investigates materials, soils and pollutants. It does not implement structure–activity design, medicinal synthesis, bioassays, structural drug modelling or experimental development.

candidateAssessment.label: Biology-focused pharmaceutical study
candidateAssessment.reason: The optional biology-focused minor supports a real direction, but VU retains the same compulsory synthesis, identification, pharmacology, toxicology, analytical and modelling sequence. Current UCR disease biology and translational methods do not supply that sustained pharmaceutical study.

audience.programmeDescription: VU Pharmaceutical Sciences studies the early stages of drug discovery through molecular biology and chemistry. Students learn to identify drug targets, design and synthesise compounds, test their activity and safety, and conduct pharmaceutical research.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers pharmacology, biochemistry and laboratory work on cells and proteins. Students can study drug targets, drug action and how the body processes medicines. VU builds on these topics with a sequence in organic synthesis, compound identification, bioanalysis, toxicology and molecular modelling for drug discovery. UCR’s available courses do not offer that sequence or a comparably sustained focus on discovering and testing new compounds.

curriculum.limitation: The 180 EC curriculum includes 30 EC of electives and an 18 EC research project. For the usual project period, students need 120 EC, all first-year courses and the specified practicals, including molecular modelling.
